pr_body:
Alt to https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/40966, fixes https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/40559

ApplicationRecord is special. If you have a multiple database
application we need to treat `ApplicationRecord` and
`ActiveRecord::Base` as the same connection, otherwise applications
will end up with duplicate connections to the same database. This is
problematic because there are a limited number of open connections an
application could have to a single database. By not treating
`ActiveRecord::Base` and `ApplicationRecord` the same we could
effectively double connections to a database (then multiplied by the
number of processes).

In the case of granular connection swapping we need to be able to read
`ApplicationRecord` off the stack while storing the
`connection_specification_name` as `ActiveRecord::Base`. In order to do
this we read the `current_preventing_writes` off the pool's
"owner_name" which was `connection_specification_name`.

To fix the issue here need to pass the original class to
`establish_connection` on the handler and then down to the `PoolConfig`.
We can then determine the `connection_specification_name` from the
`connection_klass` the same way we did in `resolve_config_for_connection`.
This isn't ideal, and I'd like to move away from the string class but
this has been part of the known API for awhile so I don't feel
comfortable changing that without investigation.

We can then read the `connection_klass` in `preventing_writes?` instead
of the connection specification name. If you're using a nil or string
value for your class, then multiple databases really won't work so
there's no point in supporting prevent writes for that.

Co-authored-by: John Crepezzi <john.crepezzi@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: alpaca-tc <alpaca-tc@alpaca.tc>

cc/ @alpaca-tc
pr_comments:
> What happen if people have a class MyApp::ApplicationRecord class in the app? This is something we should support.

We actually do this at github, we have a different one (like `ApplicationRecord::Primary`) so I hear you. We override the private primary class method that we're using here in order to achieve that. I don't want application record to be special either, but we also can't have duplicate connections open for the same database without serious consequences for some applications. I can work on making `primary_class?` part of the public API in a separate PR. Does that work?

When I said ApplicationRecord is special, I really meant "the database that Rails connects to by default needs know which one of the classes should use the equivalent primary class". In most applications this is `ApplicationRecord`. Rails _has_ to have a connection on boot and in non-eager loaded environments only `ActiveRecord::Base.establish_connection` is called on boot by the AR Railtie. In all environments that railtie would cause a duplicate connection to the first database if we didn't handle `primary_class?` to figure out which one is "special". At GitHub we override `primary_class?` but I thought that not using `ApplicationRecord` was a strange github thing. If it's more common I'll dig more into making ApplicationRecord less special in AR and giving a path forward for apps that do change their `ApplicationRecord` to something else.

> `primary_class?` part of the public API in a separate PR. Does that work?

I think so. I think we can also start to generate an ApplicationRecord setting `self.primary_class = true` instead of `self.abstract_class = true`. And `self.primary_class = true` would also set `self.abstract_class = true`.

We do have many ApplicationRecord's at Shopify. I'd say something close to 20, so I guess it is better to have an easier construction like an attribute setter for this that will take over from abstract class and also defines the database connection host.
I'll work on a separate PR to make `primary_class` part of the public API later today. 👍🏻
Working on the test failures - didn't see them because they only happen on master with the isolated test runner.

issue_context.title: preventing_writes? doesn't work in test environment
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Turn off `ActiveRecord::Base.legacy_connection_handling`
2. Use `ApplicationRecord.connects_to()`
3. include `ActiveRecord::TestFixtures`
4. Create record from inside `ApplicationRecord.connected_to(role: :reading)` block. 

https://gist.github.com/alpaca-tc/23d658d28581fddecf3b593580f9caa4

### Expected behavior

raise `ActiveRecord::ReadOnlyError`.

### Actual behavior

Nothing was raised.

### System configuration
**Rails version**: 6.1.0.rc1

**Ruby version**: 2.7.1

---

I think that the cause is  that `#replica?` now returns false because of `ActiveRecord::TestFixtures` overwritten the pool config for reading.

`preventing_writes?` checks `replica?` at the first.
https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/b60838b0ac7a9ba8ef26ef7a6abce70fbcf84f15/activerecord/lib/active_record/connection_adapters/abstract_adapter.rb#L122

`ActiveRecord::TestFixtures` removes `replica: true` option by overwriting pool config.
https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/b60838b0ac7a9ba8ef26ef7a6abce70fbcf84f15/activerecord/lib/active_record/test_fixtures.rb#L219
comments: @eileencodes I would like your opinion on this issue 😄 🙏 Is this intentional?
Thanks for the report! No this isn't intentional and revealed there's a relatively major bug in prevent writes handling. I'm working on a fix.
@eileencodes It seems that rails6.1 have been broken yet 😭 Please try to run gist code 👀

I found new related bug [gist](https://gist.github.com/alpaca-tc/f4335960b312e026808712a7f43a7947). 
I think that the abstract class that the own connection not established shouldn't swap `preventing_writes` because it can't handle [`owner_name`](https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/40615/files#diff-460f4e7973c5dd945c51d24df5b0173961190d3645f4e2585fd3003fa1fc0ff7R128).

I'll try to fix them.

review_comments: These should have always been `ActiveRecord::Base` - using primary was deprecated some time ago.

There is a slight behavior change in this public API that now accepts the class instead of a string. We could defensively handle this but applications really should be using `establish_connection` on the handler for multiple databases and this API is new in 6.1 so I think it's ok to change it. Happy to handle a string if we disagree.
